newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Westmont, Shell in fabrication deal.
newsitem.headline: Westmont, Shell in fabrication deal.

text.p: A subsidiary of Malaysia's Westmont Industries Bhd and Sabah Shell Petroleum Company Ltd on Wednesday signed a 75 million ringgit contract to build an integrated deck for a drilling platform.
Under the agreement, Westmont's wholly-owned Sabah Shipyard Sdn Bhd will carry out detailed design, fabrication, commissioning and loadout of the deck, the national Bernama news agency reported.
The deck is scheduled for installation in October next year at the Kinabalu Drilling Production Platform-A, offshore eastern Sabah state.
Located some 55 km offshore and in water depth of 55 metres, the deck will be Shell's first unmanned, remote-controlled production platform in Malaysia, Bernama said.
The 2,200-tonne deck is a three-level structure equipped with process facilities for a combined drilling and production capacity of 20 well slots.
When operational in December 1997, the platform is expected to produce 40,000 barrels of oil and 30 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.
